questions.stem: In children, inhaled foreign body is most common at which age?
What material are inhaled foreign bodies in children usually made of?
questions.answer: Organic material, such as peanuts.

questions.stem: Why is inhaled peanut particularly harmful to a child's airway?
questions.answer: It causes airway hyperreactivity.

questions.stem: Where do swallowed coins usually lodge in children?
questions.answer: The upper oesophagus.

questions.stem: In children, where does an inhaled object larger than 20 mm usually lodge?
Where does an inhaled object of 8-15 mm, or an irregular one, usually lodge?
Where do small, smooth, linear inhaled objects usually lodge?
What share of inhaled foreign bodies in children lodge in the right main bronchus?
What share of inhaled foreign bodies in children lodge in the trachea?
What are the typical presenting features of an inhaled foreign body in a child?
questions.answer: Cough, choking, drooling, wheeze, dyspnoea or cyanosis.

questions.stem: How can an inhaled foreign body in a child present when it has gone unnoticed?
questions.answer: Fever and chest infection days later, or atypical respiratory symptoms months later.

questions.stem: What examination signs suggest an inhaled foreign body in a child?
questions.answer: Airway obstruction, wheeze, reduced breath sounds.

questions.stem: In a child with an inhaled foreign body, a chest X-ray may be ____.
questions.answer: normal

questions.stem: Besides the object itself, what other chest X-ray findings can an inhaled foreign body cause in a child?
questions.answer: Lobar or lung collapse, mediastinal shift, pneumothorax.

questions.stem: What might an end-expiratory chest film show in a child with an inhaled foreign body?
questions.answer: One-sided emphysema or hyperinflation on the affected side.

questions.stem: In a child with an inhaled foreign body, under what condition are examination and removal done?
questions.answer: Under general anaesthesia.

questions.stem: What airway complication may develop after foreign body removal in children?
questions.answer: Mucosal oedema of the larynx, subglottis or trachea.

questions.stem: Preoperatively, how does respiratory distress in a child with an inhaled foreign body typically vary?
questions.answer: It varies; many children are calm.

questions.stem: What determines the urgency of removing an inhaled foreign body in a child?
questions.answer: Symptoms and degree of distress.

questions.stem: Before removal of an inhaled foreign body, can a child usually be fasted?
When should inhaled foreign body removal proceed in a child who has not fasted?
questions.answer: Partial obstruction, hypoxia or marked distress, since delay is riskier than aspiration.

questions.stem: When is laryngoscopy used to remove an inhaled foreign body?
questions.answer: When the object is in the oropharynx or near the laryngeal inlet.

questions.stem: What premedication is given before laryngoscopy for an inhaled foreign body in a child?
In laryngoscopy for an inhaled foreign body, what is the aim?
questions.answer: A patent airway with spontaneous breathing throughout.

questions.stem: For laryngoscopy in an inhaled foreign body case, which induction agent and oxygen mix is used?
questions.answer: Halothane or sevoflurane in 100% oxygen.

questions.stem: When upper airway obstruction slows inhalational induction in a child, what helps?
questions.answer: Gentle CPAP.

questions.stem: Once a child is deep enough for laryngoscopy, what atropine dose is given?
Once a child is deep enough for laryngoscopy, what glycopyrronium dose is given instead?
How should a child be positioned for bronchoscopy to bring the trachea forward?
questions.answer: Supine, with a roll under the scapulae.

questions.stem: Why spray the vocal cords with lidocaine before bronchoscopy in a child?
questions.answer: Dense laryngeal topicalisation prevents coughing and breath holding.

questions.stem: What is the maximum lidocaine dose sprayed on the vocal cords before bronchoscopy in a child?
Which breathing circuit attaches to the side arm of a Storz bronchoscope?
questions.answer: A T-piece circuit.

questions.stem: What is the maintenance technique for bronchoscopy in children?
questions.answer: Volatile agent in 100% oxygen, with spontaneous ventilation preferred.

questions.stem: Why can inserting the telescope be a problem during bronchoscopy in infants?
questions.answer: It narrows the lumen and greatly increases work of breathing.

questions.stem: After foreign body removal, how should the endotracheal tube size compare with the age-based size?
How should a child be extubated after bronchoscopy for foreign body removal?
questions.answer: Awake.

questions.stem: What dexamethasone dose is often given IV to reduce airway oedema after bronchoscopy?
After bronchoscopy, where should a child with significant airway oedema be kept?
questions.answer: Intubated and ventilated in ICU.

questions.stem: After oesophagoscopy or OGD for a foreign body, how is the child extubated?
What serious complication is a risk after rigid oesophagoscopy in children?
questions.answer: Oesophageal perforation.

questions.stem: After removal of an inhaled foreign body, where do most children go?
Where is a child with stridor after foreign body removal observed?
What nebulised 1:1000 adrenaline dose is used for post-extraction stridor?
How long does nebulised adrenaline relieve stridor from mucosal oedema after foreign body removal?
After bronchoscopy, at what interval can dexamethasone 100 mcg/kg IV be given for 24 hours?
After foreign body removal in a child, what fluid is given until the child is drinking?
questions.answer: IV maintenance fluids.

questions.stem: When are antibiotics given after foreign body removal in a child?
questions.answer: If late presentation with infection.
